must_fix.title: Live announcers/top-layer elements inside the shadow root of a host added after ariaHideOutside runs are hidden, unlike the light DOM
must_fix.evidence: The MutationObserver calls walk(addedNode), which finds announcers only via root.querySelectorAll and doesn't look inside shadow roots, so the new host is aria-hidden along with the announcer in its shadow root. A scratch jest probe with enableShadowDOM() printed `LIGHT wrapper hidden= null ann= null` for a light-DOM wrapper with a [data-live-announcer] child, and `SHADOW host hidden= true ann= null` for a host whose shadow root holds the same announcer. The issue requires announcers and top-layer elements to stay visible 'as they do in the light DOM'. No test covers this case.

nits: With the flag on, getShadowLiveElements walks the whole root with a shadow tree walker and calls matches() on every element on every modal/popover/combobox open, even on pages with no shadow roots. Consider a cheaper check or limiting the walk to subtrees that actually contain shadow hosts.

The flag-off test in ariaHideOutside.test.js only checks that the shadow sibling isn't hidden. It could also check that a light-DOM sibling is still hidden, to show the light-DOM behavior is unchanged.

report:
**Verdict: not ready to merge.** One bug goes against what the issue asks for. Tests, lint and the type check all pass. **Checks run** - `yarn jest packages/@react-aria/overlays`: all 11 suites and 199 tests pass. - `yarn eslint packages/@react-aria/overlays`: no errors. - `yarn check-types`: exits 0. - The new `@react-stately/flags` dependency uses `^3.1.2`, the same range as the other four `@react-aria` packages that depend on it, and `yarn.lock` matches. **Must fix: a live announcer or top-layer element is hidden if its shadow host is added after the call** The issue says content added later should be hidden, but live announcers and top-layer elements must stay visible "as they do in the light DOM." When the observer sees a new node, it calls `walk(node)`. That function only finds announcers with `root.querySelectorAll(...)` (`ariaHideOutside.ts`, in `walk`), and `querySelectorAll` doesn't look inside the new node's shadow root. So the new host gets `aria-hidden="true"`, and the announcer inside its shadow root is hidden along with it. A real case: a web component holding a toast region or live announcer that mounts after a modal opens. I wrote a scratch test (deleted afterwards) that runs with `enableShadowDOM()` on and compares the two cases: - Light DOM: append `
` to `body` after `ariaHideOutside([t])`. - Shadow DOM: append a host whose shadow root holds the same announcer. ``` $ yarn jest packages/@react-aria/overlays/test/zzprobe.test.js LIGHT wrapper hidden= null ann= null SHADOW host hidden= true ann= null ``` In the light DOM the wrapper stays visible, so the announcer can still be heard. In the shadow DOM the host is hidden, so the announcer is cut off. The fix: when the observer walks an added subtree, also look through the shadow roots inside it with `getShadowLiveElements`, keep the hosts on the way to any announcer it finds, and observe those shadow roots. A test for this case should be added next to the existing "should keep live announcers…" tests. **What I checked that works** - Siblings are hidden in nested shadow roots, and the hosts on the path stay visible. - Light-DOM children of a host that has a slotted target are hidden. - Targets in different shadow roots both stay visible. - Content added later to a shadow root on the path is hidden. - Cleanup restores everything and stops observing. - Nested calls pause and then resume the outer observer. - A `root` inside a shadow root doesn't hide anything above it. - With the flag off, nothing changes. Adding an announcer to an existing shadow root that encloses no target leaves it hidden.
